title: How to transfer an eSIM from one iPhone to another
summary: Transfer an eSIM from one iPhone to another in a few taps, with no carrier visit and no lost number. See the full steps. Start your transfer.
body_markdown:
Your new iPhone is on the table, and your phone number lives on the old one as an eSIM. There’s no SIM tray to open and no card to slide across, so it isn’t obvious how to transfer an eSIM from one iPhone to another without losing service. The answer depends on your carrier and on which version of iOS both phones are running. This guide covers the quick route, the route for after setup, the fixes when it fails, and what changes for travel eSIMs.


You can move an eSIM between iPhones with eSIM Quick Transfer, during setup or later in Settings. On the new iPhone, choose Transfer From Nearby iPhone, then tap Transfer on the old one. Both iPhones need iOS 18.4 or later, Bluetooth on and a carrier that supports Quick Transfer. If yours doesn't, your carrier can issue a QR code.


## What is eSIM Quick Transfer on iPhone?


eSIM Quick Transfer is an iPhone feature that moves your phone number's eSIM from your previous iPhone to your new one over a nearby connection, so in many cases you don't need to ask your carrier for a new QR code. It's the quickest way to complete an eSIM transfer on iPhone, but it only works when your carrier supports it.


Per[Apple's eSIM instructions](https://support.apple.com/en-us/118669) , you need all of the following:


- Both iPhones signed in with your Apple Account.
- Both iPhones on iOS 18.4 or later. Transferring more than one phone number at once requires iOS 26 or later.
- The previous iPhone unlocked with its passcode.
- Both iPhones nearby, with Bluetooth on.
- A Wi-Fi network or hotspot. Some eSIM-only models in certain countries can activate without one.
- A carrier that supports eSIM Quick Transfer.


Quick Transfer appears during setup if you’re asked to transfer your phone number to the new iPhone. If you skip that prompt or your iPhone is already set up, you can start the transfer later in Settings. If neither option appears, your carrier probably doesn’t support Quick Transfer, so use the QR code route in the troubleshooting section.


If either iPhone is on older software, update it first. Check with your carrier too: support depends on the carrier, not only on the phones.


## How to transfer an eSIM during iPhone setup


To transfer an eSIM during setup, turn on the new iPhone, follow the prompts until it asks you to transfer your phone number, and approve the transfer on your previous iPhone. Keep both phones close together and unlocked, with Bluetooth on, until the new plan activates. These steps use Apple’s wording for the buttons:


**1. Start setup on the new iPhone.** Follow the setup screens and sign in with your Apple Account when asked. Keep the previous iPhone nearby, unlocked and connected to Wi-Fi. **‍**


**2. Reach the cellular screen.** When the new iPhone asks you to set up cellular or to transfer your phone number, choose to transfer from your previous iPhone. If no list of numbers appears, tap **Transfer From Nearby iPhone** .


**3. Choose the plan to move.** If you have several numbers, pick the one you want to transfer.


**4. Confirm on the previous iPhone.** Follow the instructions that appear on it and tap **Transfer** . If it asks for a verification code, enter the code shown on the new iPhone.


**5. Wait for the plan to activate.** Activating the plan on the new iPhone deactivates the SIM on the previous one, so don’t switch the old phone off in the middle of the transfer.


**6. Finish with your carrier if asked.** If a banner reads **Finish Setting Up Your Carrier’s Cellular Plan** , tap it and complete the transfer on your carrier’s website.


**7. Test the line.** Make a call from the new iPhone to confirm it has service.


Apple’s page doesn’t spell out the setup screens word-for-word, so the labels you see may vary slightly across iOS versions and carriers. The Quick Transfer buttons themselves, Transfer From Nearby iPhone and Transfer, match Apple’s instructions. If you transfer several numbers at once, make sure both iPhones run iOS 26 or later.


## How to transfer an eSIM after setup is finished


If your new iPhone is already set up, you can move the eSIM from Settings by going to Cellular, then Add eSIM, and choosing a plan to transfer from your previous iPhone. This is the route to use if you skipped the prompt during setup or recently got a new iPhone. The same requirements apply: both iPhones running iOS 18.4 or later, Bluetooth and Wi-Fi on, and a carrier that supports Quick Transfer. To move an eSIM to a new iPhone this way:


1. Open **Settings** on the new iPhone and tap **Cellular** . In some regions, this menu is called “ **Mobile”** or “ **Mobile Data”** .


2. Tap **Set Up Cellular** or **Add eSIM** .


3. Choose a plan to transfer from another iPhone. If no list of numbers appears, tap **Transfer From Nearby iPhone** .


4. On the previous iPhone, follow the prompts and tap **Transfer** , or enter the verification code shown on the new iPhone if prompted.


5. Wait for the plan to activate on the new iPhone. This deactivates the SIM on the previous one.


6. If a banner reads **Finish Setting Up Your Carrier’s Cellular Plan** , tap it. You’ll be redirected to your carrier’s website to complete the transfer.


When it’s done, return to **Settings** and **Cellular** to check that the plan is listed. If you have two plans on the same iPhone, both will appear there. Then call someone to confirm the line works.


## Why is my eSIM transfer not working?


An eSIM transfer usually fails because your carrier doesn’t support Quick Transfer, or because one of the requirements isn’t met: Bluetooth is off, an iPhone is on an older iOS, or the phones aren’t signed in to the same Apple Account. Work through these checks in order, then fall back to your carrier’s QR code if the transfer still won’t start.


- **Carrier support:** Quick Transfer only appears if your carrier supports it. Ask your carrier, or check its website, before you spend time troubleshooting.
- **Carrier lock:** If the new iPhone is locked to a different carrier, it may not accept your plan. Ask your carrier to confirm the iPhone is unlocked.
- **Bluetooth off:** Both iPhones need Bluetooth on and need to be close together.
- **iOS version mismatch:** Both iPhones must run iOS 18.4 or later. Update the one that's behind.
- **Apple Account or lock screen:** Both iPhones must be signed in with your Apple Account, and the previous iPhone must be unlocked with its passcode.
- **No Wi-Fi:** Connect both iPhones to Wi-Fi, or use a hotspot, then try again.
- **Carrier step unfinished:** If a banner says “ **Finish Setting Up Your Carrier’s Cellular Plan** ,” tap it to complete the transfer on your carrier’s web page.


If none of these fixes it, use the QR code route, which doesn’t depend on Quick Transfer. Ask your carrier for a QR code, then use one of these methods:


- **During setup:** Tap **Use QR code** on the Set Up Cellular screen and follow the prompts.
- **After setup:** Scan the code with the Camera app, then tap the **Cellular Plan Detected** notification. Your carrier may give you a confirmation code to enter.
- **Carrier link:** On iOS 17.4 or later, tap the link your carrier sends, then tap **Allow i** n the **Activate New eSIM** notification.
- **Manual entry:** In Settings, tap **Add Cellular Plan** , then tap **Enter Details Manually** .


Some carriers also let you transfer your number in their own app. If the transfer still fails, contact your carrier: it can see what’s happening on your account.


## Travel eSIMs versus carrier eSIMs when you switch phones


A carrier eSIM is linked to your phone number, so Quick Transfer or your carrier can move it to a new iPhone, whereas a travel eSIM is a data plan installed via a QR code and may not move at all. The difference matters if you’re changing phones before or during a trip. A QR code for a travel plan, which is the eSIM QR code iPhone owners scan to install it, is a profile for one device, not a number that travels with you.

Phone number Keeps your number for calls and texts Usually data only, so it won't receive calls or texts to your number

If you’re about to switch phones during a trip, don’t delete a travel eSIM from the old iPhone until you know whether the provider can reissue it. ## Frequently asked questions


### Can I transfer an eSIM without contacting my carrier?


Yes, if your carrier supports eSIM Quick Transfer and both iPhones meet Apple’s requirements. You then move the plan from the new iPhone and approve it on the old one. If your carrier doesn’t support Quick Transfer, you’ll need a QR code or a transfer through its app.


### Does transferring an eSIM delete it from my old iPhone?


It stops working there. Apple says activating the plan on the new iPhone deactivates your previous SIM, but its instructions don’t say whether the eSIM is removed from the old iPhone’s settings. Check that the new iPhone has service before you reset or sell the old one.


### Can I transfer an eSIM from an iPhone to an Android phone?


Sometimes.[Apple says](https://support.apple.com/en-us/123878) that with iOS 26 and later, some carriers and select smartphone manufacturers support moving a SIM between Android and iPhone, in either direction. Otherwise, contact your carrier for a new eSIM.


### What happens to my travel eSIM data plan when I switch phones?


It depends on the provider. A travel eSIM is activated via a QR code that many providers offer on one device only, so the plan may not transfer with the phone. Contact the provider before deleting it from the old iPhone and ask whether it can issue a new code.


### Do I need Wi-Fi to transfer an eSIM?


Usually, yes. Apple lists a Wi-Fi network or hotspot among its requirements, though some eSIM-only iPhone models in certain countries can activate without one. Both iPhones also need Bluetooth on.


### Can I have two eSIMs active on one iPhone?


Yes, on iPhone 13 and later, according to[Apple’s Dual SIM guidance](https://support.apple.com/en-us/109317) . Earlier models pair one eSIM with a physical SIM. Your iPhone uses only one cellular data network at a time.
